1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter and line spacing on all screens.

2.why: Text is sentence-case, non-italic, and limited to short labels and one-line descriptions with no dense blocks or all-caps.

3.why: Layout is single-column with large controls and appears well adapted to a mobile viewport.

4.why: Copy such as 'Sign in to continue' and 'Confirm your account details before setting up payment security' is short and plain.

5.why: Email and mobile fields display example values as placeholders and a note tells the user to use those details.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long paragraph; all instructional text is one sentence or less.

7.why: No long codes or secrets are ever shown, so copy-versus-type support cannot be observed.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry appears in any screenshot.

9.why: Standard email and tel input fields are used that normally support browser autofill and password managers, though MFA-code fields are never reached.

10.why: The heading 'Sign in to continue' and the large blue Continue button clearly indicate the current step and primary action.

11.why: Only one primary action (the Continue button) is presented on the form.

12.why: After Continue the only feedback is the generic banner 'We could not complete that request. Please try again,' which does not explain what happened or what comes next.

13.why: The form stays usable after the error so the user can retry Continue with no lockout; no codes are present to reveal or re-request.

14.why: The error text is generic, does not identify the actual problem or a concrete fix, although it avoids blaming the user.

15.why: No time limits are displayed or mentioned on any screen; code-entry timing cannot be assessed because that step is never reached.
